subject: 🧭 Asana's new sidebar: what moved, and the new Knowledge tab

Before we jump into this week's content, two Asanathon updates.

 

First, the date has moved. Asanathon 2026 now runs on Thursday, October 8. Free, live online, and the replay goes to everyone who registers.

 

Second, the full agenda is now up on the page. Spencer Herrick, AI Product Lead at Asana, joins us for a panel on where agentic AI is heading and what to expect to see in your own Asana environment soon 👀 Marquis emcees, and Juli and Claara runs the hands-on workshop, with a limited number of demo seats for anyone who wants to build alongside us.

 

👉 See the agenda and save your spot

 

Now onto this week's content 👇

🎥 ASANA'S NEW SIDEBAR MENU: WHAT MOVED WHERE

If you've opened Asana in the last few days, the sidebar looks different. Five tabs now instead of four, and the one that used to be called Workflows is now Agents.

 

This week's video walks the whole thing, tab by tab, so you know where your work went.

 

We cover:

  • Work, holding home, inbox, my tasks, timesheets, projects and portfolios, plus why Starred is the better habit than the full project list
  • Agents, which now separates AI teammates from workflows, with their own pages for rules, forms, templates and custom fields
  • the forms page, which finally shows every form in one list with its creator, its access, its submission count and the project it lives in
  • Strategy, pulling goals, reporting and resourcing into one place
  • Knowledge, the new tab, with Pages for SOPs and shared resources, and Meetings sitting behind a waitlist

If you have ever gone hunting for a form by opening six projects in a row, the forms page alone is worth the tour 👇

Watch the Full Sidebar Tour

📝 ASANA DASHBOARDS AND REPORTING: THE COMPLETE GUIDE

Someone asks where things stand. You open the Dashboard tab, Asana has helpfully pre-populated tasks by assignee and a count of overdue work, and none of it answers the question you were actually asked. That is the moment most people decide Asana's reporting is limited.

 

Our very own Juli's new guide is the long answer to why it usually is not. It covers:

  • the three levels of reporting, project, portfolio and universal, and how to pick the right one for the question you were asked
  • the four decisions behind every chart in the builder
  • ten dashboard configurations you can copy, from executive portfolio health to where the hours actually go
  • a straight list of what Asana reporting cannot do, so you don't spend a week building something that was never going to work

One correction it makes on the way through: duration is chartable. Average time in a section, or in a custom field value, which is how “approvals feel slow” turns into “approvals average six days and everything else averages one.”

 

Goals reporting gets its own write-up, which Juli published earlier this month.

READ FULL BLOG POST

In Case You Missed it:

  • 🎥 Build two AI teammates with us
  • 📝 Shadow AI in our own company: 15 tools, 3 approved
  • 🎥 What's new in Asana: the new rules updates
  • 📁 Asana templates you might like
